outcome: The full claim (every bridgeless graph with no Petersen-graph minor has a nowhere-zero 4-flow) is still open as far as the sources show. Two 2026 arXiv preprints bear on it: Pintér (arXiv 2607.22267, first posted 24 Jul 2026) proves the result only for graphs excluding a proper minor of the Petersen graph, and Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe (arXiv 2608.22870, 24 Aug 2026) claim to complete the cubic special case (Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture) through a computer-assisted apex proof, with no public engagement found.
problem_asks: One universal claim, stated over all finite bridgeless graphs G: if G has no Petersen-graph minor (P, the Petersen graph on 10 vertices), then G admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Parts: (1) the class: bridgeless graphs with no P minor (the bullet says 'graph'; several sources state the result for multigraphs, which is the wider setting); (2) the conclusion: a nowhere-zero 4-flow (for this purpose equivalent to a nowhere-zero Z_2^2-flow). There is no cubic or planar restriction in the bullet. The cubic case, where a nowhere-zero 4-flow is equivalent to 3-edge-colourability (Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture for 2-connected cubic graphs with no P minor), is a special case of the same claim, not a separate part. The bullet is settled only by covering every graph in the class; a result on a proper subclass leaves it open.

events.what_happened: Kilakos and Shepherd, 'Excluding minors in cubic graphs', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing 5 (1996) 57-78 (doi 10.1017/S0963548300001838). Known only from secondary sources read in search snippets; the paper was not opened. Per those snippets, it shows that cubic (3-regular) graphs with no P10 minor (P10 = P minus an edge, per the Thomas–Thomson convention) have nowhere-zero 4-flows, and Thomas and Thomson later removed the cubic hypothesis.
events.delivers: Per secondary sources only: nowhere-zero 4-flows for cubic bridgeless graphs with no P10 minor (P minus an edge). A proper-minor class, restricted to cubic graphs.
events.remains: The Petersen-minor-free class itself (P not excluded). Non-cubic graphs. Graphs with a P10 minor and no P minor.

checked_by.who: Editorial process of Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (refereed journal)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result; the referee process is not visible from the sources read.
checked_by.what_they_did: Published the paper in 1996 (volume and pages from the search snippet and DOI).

events.time_since_posted: 30 years (no later engagement with the paper itself was examined)
events.doubts: Not opened; the statement and the 'P10' convention rest on one secondary snippet and on the Thomas–Thomson abstract, which describes Kilakos–Shepherd as covering 3-regular graphs. Whether the 1996 result concerns P or P10 is not verified from the primary text.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive result) for a restricted class: cubic graphs with no P10 minor.

events.what_happened: Announcement (no written argument located) that Sanders and Thomas had proved that every 2-edge-connected apex cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable, the apex half of the Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas programme. Robin Thomas's homepage lists 'D. P. Sanders, P. D. Seymour and R. Thomas, Edge 3-coloring cubic apex graphs, in preparation'. The Inoue et al. 2026 preprint says the apex part 'has never been published, although a proof was announced by Sanders and Thomas around 30 years ago'. A 2016 Princeton mailing-list post reports that Sanders and Thomas 'recently solved' the apex case. These sources disagree on timing and on status, so the date is given to the year only and approximate.
events.delivers: As announced: every 2-edge-connected apex cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable (cubic case, apex graphs only). No written argument is available to read, so what is delivered is the claim, not a verified result.
events.remains: Everything, as far as any written source shows: the apex case is the piece later claimed by Inoue et al. (2026). Non-cubic graphs remain untouched.
events.time_since_posted: about 30 years, with no written argument located
events.doubts: No written proof located. The Thomas page lists the paper as 'in preparation' (no date). The 2026 preprint says it was never published. The 2016 mailing-list post says 'recently solved', which conflicts with both. The claim may be the same proof that the 2026 preprint now presents, but the sources do not establish that.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive claim) for the apex cubic subcase.

events.what_happened: Robertson, Seymour and Thomas, 'Tutte's edge-colouring conjecture', J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 70 (1997) 166-183 (May 1997 issue). Per the Princeton publication listing and Thomas's homepage, this paper is one of the five papers of the programme announced by Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas. It shows that Tutte's conjecture (every 2-connected cubic graph with no P minor is 3-edge-colourable) holds in general if it holds for two special classes of cubic graphs close to planar, the apex graphs and the doublecross graphs. The Princeton abstract text was read only as a search snippet; the paper itself was not opened.
events.delivers: A reduction, not a colouring result: the cubic special case (2-connected cubic graphs with no P minor, equivalent to nowhere-zero 4-flow for cubic graphs) follows if every 2-connected apex cubic graph and every doublecross cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable. Restricted to cubic graphs.
events.remains: Both reduction classes (apex and doublecross) and the entire non-cubic class, which the reduction does not address.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B (refereed)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the result.

checked_by.who: Edwards, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, and then Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe
checked_by.qualification: Authors of the later pieces of the programme; Inoue et al. cite the reduction as 'Theorem 1.3' and treat it as established.
checked_by.what_they_did: Relied on the reduction in their own papers (2016 and 2026). This is reliance, not an independent check.

events.doubts: The Snark article on Wikipedia says the complete proof of the RSST programme 'remains unpublished' and that steps appeared in 2016 and 2019, so the reduction's published status as a whole is disputed. The 1997 paper is one of five papers and only that one is cited as published on Thomas's homepage.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive), conditionally: it reduces the cubic case to two classes. It asserts no counterexample.

events.what_happened: Announcement of a complete proof of Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture (cubic special case of the bullet) by Robertson, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas. The Snark article on Wikipedia dates it to 1999 and says 'steps towards this result have been published in 2016 and 2019, but the complete proof remains unpublished'. Thomas's homepage gives the same announcement without a date and says the proof 'will be published in' five papers. No written complete argument was located.
events.delivers: As announced: the cubic case (2-connected cubic graphs with no P minor are 3-edge-colourable). Claimed only; no complete written argument located.
events.remains: The announced complete proof, which has not been published as one piece according to the Snark article. Non-cubic graphs remain untouched.
events.time_since_posted: 27 years, with no complete written argument located
events.doubts: The announcement date conflicts across sources (1996–1997 in the 2026 preprint's account of the apex history, 1999 on Wikipedia). The complete proof has not been published according to the Snark article.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive claim) for the cubic subcase.

events.what_happened: Kochol, 'Cubic graphs without a Petersen minor have nowhere-zero 5-flows', Acta Mathematica Universitatis Comenianae 68(2) (1999) 249-252. Known from a search snippet and an EMIS listing; the paper itself was not opened (the EMIS abstract page returned HTTP 503, the PDF was unreadable here). Its result, per the snippet: every bridgeless cubic graph with no Petersen minor has a nowhere-zero 5-flow.
events.delivers: A nowhere-zero 5-flow, not a 4-flow, for bridgeless cubic graphs with no Petersen minor. This is an analogue of the bullet with a weaker flow value, restricted to cubic graphs.
events.remains: The 4-flow claim for the same class (the cubic case of the bullet is the stronger 4-flow version). Non-cubic graphs.
events.doubts: Not opened; the content rests on a search snippet and on a later summary that calls the 5-flow result an approximation of the 4-flow conjecture. A search summary also says a 4-flow follows from the later Robertson–Sanders–Seymour–Thomas theorem, which is what makes Kochol's 5-flow weaker.
events.direction: Cuts toward Tutte's flow programme (positive, weaker value): nowhere-zero 5-flows for cubic P-minor-free graphs.

events.what_happened: Thomas and Thomson, 'Excluding minors in nonplanar graphs of girth at least five', Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (Cambridge listing: copyright 2000, online 2001). Per the abstract as quoted in search snippets (the paper was not opened): every quasi 4-connected nonplanar graph with minimum degree at least three and no cycle shorter than five has a minor isomorphic to P10 (P minus an edge). A stated consequence is that every 2-edge-connected graph with no P10 minor has a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Pintér builds on this girth-five framework.
events.delivers: Nowhere-zero 4-flows for 2-edge-connected graphs with no P10 (= P minus an edge) minor. A proper-minor class; not cubic-restricted.
events.remains: The Petersen-minor-free class: P is not excluded, so graphs containing a P10 minor and no P minor are not in the bullet's class, but graphs with P10 minor are outside this result; the bullet's full class is not covered.

checked_by.who: Cambridge University Press editorial process for Combinatorics, Probability and Computing (refereed journal)

checked_by.qualification: Author of the 2026 preprint, which cites the result as a known input.
checked_by.what_they_did: Relies on it in his proof (reliance, not an independent check).

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive) for the proper-minor class R = P minus an edge.

events.what_happened: I. Cahit, 'Spiral Chains: The Proofs of Tait's and Tutte's Three-Edge-Coloring Conjectures', arXiv math/0507127, v1 6 Jul 2005, labelled 'draft-paper, 14 pages, 8 figures'. The abstract says the method shows, without the four-colour theorem, that every bridgeless cubic planar graph is 3-edge-colourable, and says the method has 'applicability' to Tutte's conjecture that every 2-connected cubic graph with no Petersen minor is 3-edge-colourable. The title claims a proof of Tutte's conjecture; the abstract's own wording is weaker. Only one arXiv version is listed.
events.revisions: v1 6 Jul 2005 only (as shown on the arXiv abstract page read).
events.delivers: As claimed: a non-computer route to 3-edge-colouring of cubic P-minor-free graphs (the cubic subcase), with the abstract's own wording only saying the method is 'applicable' to it. Not checked by anyone.
events.remains: Everything, if the claim is not valid: the cubic subcase and the whole bullet.
events.doubts: Draft-status preprint, single version, no journal publication found, no reviews or responses found in searches. The abstract's claim about Tutte's conjecture is an 'applicability' claim, not a stated theorem. The title's claim conflicts with that wording.
events.direction: Claimed cuts toward the conjecture (positive), for the cubic subcase; unverified.

events.what_happened: Taoye Zhang's 2007 WVU PhD dissertation 'Integer flow and Petersen minor' (chapter 1) proves that every bridgeless graph with no P-with-three-matching-edges-contracted minor (P/3, the Petersen graph with three edges of a perfect matching contracted) admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow. The same result is published as Wang, Zhang and Zhang, 'Nowhere-zero 4-flow in almost Petersen-minor free graphs', Discrete Mathematics 309(5) (2009) 1025-1032 (doi 10.1016/j.disc.2007.11.055). Dated to the 2007 dissertation as the first public written argument. The Discrete Mathematics paper was not opened; the dissertation was read via its repository record.
events.revisions: Journal version in Discrete Mathematics 309(5) (2009) 1025-1032; a 2008 online date appears in one listing.
events.delivers: Nowhere-zero 4-flows for bridgeless graphs with no P/3 minor. Because P has P/3 as a minor, P/3-minor-free graphs are a subclass of P-minor-free graphs, so this covers a proper subclass of the bullet's class.
events.remains: Bridgeless graphs with no P minor that do contain a P/3 minor. This includes the Petersen-minor-free graphs not already covered, and thus the bullet's class in full.

checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the 2009 version.
Cites the result in his 2026 preprint as prior work.
checked_by.what_they_did: Cites it (reliance, not an independent check).

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive) for the proper-subclass P/3-minor-free class.

events.what_happened: Robertson, Seymour and Thomas, 'Excluded minors in cubic graphs', arXiv 1403.2118 (v1 9 Mar 2014; 62 pages), published in J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 138 (2019) 219-285 per MathWorld. A structural step in the RSST programme. Per its abstract (read in part): for cubic graphs of girth at least five with a condition on vertex partitions and no homeomorphic embedding of the Petersen graph (and not one specific 20-vertex graph), either deleting a vertex leaves a planar graph or the graph can be drawn in the plane with only two crossings, both on the infinite region.
events.revisions: v1 9 Mar 2014; journal version JCTB 138 (2019) 219-285 per MathWorld.
events.delivers: A structural classification of certain cubic graphs with no P topological embedding (apex-like or two-crossing-drawable). It states no edge-colouring conclusion in the abstract read, so it is a structural input, not a colouring result.
events.remains: The 3-edge-colouring claim itself (the cubic subcase of the bullet) and the whole bullet.

checked_by.who: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B (refereed)
checked_by.qualification: Journal of record for the 2019 version.

events.doubts: Its precise role in the reduction is not stated in the abstract read; the link to the apex and doublecross classes is inferred from the programme's structure, not from this abstract.
events.direction: Structural; does not cut toward or against the conjecture on its own.

events.what_happened: Edwards, Sanders, Seymour and Thomas, 'Three-edge-colouring doublecross cubic graphs', arXiv 1411.4352 (v1 17 Nov 2014; latest revision v3 30 Nov 2015), published in J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 119 (2016) 66-95. Per the abstract (read in excerpt): every two-edge-connected doublecross cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable, where doublecross means drawable in the plane with only two crossings, both on the infinite region. The motivating question is Tutte's conjecture on cubic graphs with no Petersen minor; the paper does not study Petersen minors directly. The proof is a variant of the four-colour theorem proof.
events.delivers: The doublecross subcase of the cubic reduction: 2-edge-connected doublecross cubic graphs are 3-edge-colourable. Restricted to doublecross cubic graphs, so a class strictly smaller than the cubic bullet case.
events.remains: The apex cubic case (needed with it for the reduction), and the non-cubic class of the bullet.

Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe (2026)
checked_by.qualification: Authors of the 2026 apex preprint, which relies on this result.

events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive) for the doublecross cubic subcase.

events.what_happened: Robertson, Seymour and Thomas, 'Cyclically five-connected cubic graphs', arXiv 1503.02298 (v1 8 Mar 2015; 'revised according to referee's comments, to appear in JCTB'), published J. Combin. Theory Ser. B 125 (2017) 132-167 per Thomas's homepage. Per the abstract (read in summary): a topological containment result for cyclically 5-connected cubic graphs, giving a reduction step in which a graph G is obtained from a cubic graph H by one of two specified operations.
events.delivers: A topological containment lemma for cyclically 5-connected cubic graphs; the abstract does not state a 3-edge-colouring or nowhere-zero flow conclusion.
events.remains: The colouring claim and the whole bullet.

events.doubts: The abstract does not state a link to Petersen minors or to the colouring conjecture; any link is inferred from the programme's structure.
events.direction: Structural; does not cut toward or against the conjecture on its own.

events.what_happened: Mkrtchyan, 'Sublinear bounds for nullity of flows and approximating Tutte's flow conjectures', arXiv 2008.07152 (v1 17 Aug 2020). Per the abstract (read in summary): it states equivalences between Tutte's flow conjectures and sublinear nullity bounds for abelian flows that need not be nowhere-zero, including one for bridgeless graphs with no P minor. It proves no nowhere-zero 4-flow result. The v2 (7 Oct 2020) is marked withdrawn, and the comments say the results were previously obtained by Kochol (2002).
events.revisions: v1 17 Aug 2020; v2 7 Oct 2020 marked withdrawn.
events.delivers: An equivalence between the 4-flow conjecture for P-minor-free bridgeless graphs and a sublinear nullity bound for abelian flows. It does not deliver a nowhere-zero 4-flow for any class.
events.doubts: Withdrawn; the comments say the content was previously obtained by Kochol (2002), which I did not open.

withdrawn.what: arXiv 2008.07152 v2 (7 Oct 2020) is marked withdrawn; the comments say the results were previously obtained by Kochol (2002). The party withdrawing is not shown on the abstract page read.

events.direction: No direction on the bullet's nowhere-zero claim; the statement is an equivalence of a different (non-nowhere-zero) form.

events.what_happened: Wang, Zhang and Zhou (author order is disputed across sources; the journal listing gives 'Wang, Zhang, Zhou'), 'On Nowhere Zero 4-Flows in Regular Matroids', Theory and Applications of Graphs 10(2) (2023) article 1, pp. 1-9, DOI 10.20429/tag.2023.100201. The result (per the search summary; the journal article was not opened): a co-loopless regular matroid avoiding the matroids of P/3 and of the dual of K5 admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow; the P/3 matroid is the matroid analogue of the graph class in the 2009 paper.
events.delivers: A matroid-level analogue: nowhere-zero 4-flows for co-loopless regular matroids with no P/3-matroid minor. It concerns matroids, not the graph bullet.
events.remains: The graph bullet entirely. It is discounted as a different question (matroids rather than graphs).
events.doubts: Not opened; relies on search-result summaries and the repository record. The journal listing and author order conflict across sources.
events.direction: Analogue, not the bullet: cuts toward a matroid version of the 4-flow claim.

events.what_happened: Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe, 'Three-edge-coloring projective planar cubic graphs: a generalization of the Four Color Theorem', arXiv 2405.16586 (submitted 26 May 2024). Per the arXiv abstract page (read in summary; full text not read): every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph embeddable in the projective plane is 3-edge-colourable, with the Petersen graph as the only exception, and a 2-edge-connected projective-planar graph admits a nowhere-zero 4-flow unless it is 'Petersen-like'. Uses computer verification. The abstract does not mention Petersen-minor-free graphs.
events.revisions: v1 26 May 2024; a later listing (ResearchGate) shows a publication record not checked here.
events.delivers: Results for projective-planar graphs, which are a different hypothesis (embeddability) from the bullet's (P-minor-freeness). Petersen itself is projective-planar and is the exception, so this is not a subclass of the bullet's class. Discounted as an analogue.
events.doubts: Full text not opened; based on the abstract page and search-result summaries.
events.direction: Analogue, different hypothesis: 3-edge-colouring and nowhere-zero 4-flows for projective-planar graphs; the only exception is the Petersen graph.

events.what_happened: Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe, 'Three-edge-coloring (Tait coloring) cubic graphs on the torus: a proof of Grünbaum's conjecture', arXiv 2505.07002 (submitted 11 May 2025). Per the abstract page (read in summary; full text not read): every cyclically 4-edge-connected cubic graph embeddable in the torus is 3-edge-colourable, except a 'Petersen-like' class built from copies of P (toroidal snarks). Mentions extensive computer verification. It does not state AI use.
events.revisions: v1 11 May 2025; an arXiv admin note records text overlap with arXiv:2405.16586.
events.delivers: Results for toroidal cubic graphs, a different hypothesis (embeddability) from the bullet's. The torus contains P, so the class is not a subclass of the bullet's. Discounted as an analogue.
events.direction: Analogue, different hypothesis: 3-edge-colouring of toroidal cubic graphs, with the Petersen-like class as exception.

events.what_happened: József Pintér (Department of Stochastics, Institute of Mathematics, Budapest University of Technology and Economics), arXiv 2607.22267, first posted 24 Jul 2026 (UTC 13:03) under the title 'Nowhere-zero 4-flows in graphs excluding the Petersen graph with one edge contracted'. Main theorem (Theorem 1.1 of v1, read via the arXiv HTML): every finite bridgeless undirected multigraph with no Q minor admits a nowhere-zero Z_2^2-flow, hence a nowhere-zero 4-flow, where Q = P/e (P the Petersen graph, e an edge). The abstract: every almost 4-connected nonplanar graph of minimum degree at least three and girth at least five contains P/e as a minor; the finite part is computer-assisted and verifies the required minor models in the Petersen, Triplex and Basket graphs and in the jump and facial cross extensions of the Dodecahedron. Version 2 (9 Aug 2026) is retitled 'Nowhere-zero 4-flows in graphs excluding a proper minor of the Petersen graph', states the conjecture in the bullet's form in its abstract, and adds that combining the result with Thomas and Thomson's theorem for (P−e)-minor-free graphs covers every proper minor R of P. The paper does not claim to prove the full conjecture.
events.revisions: v1 24 Jul 2026 (title 'Nowhere-zero 4-flows in graphs excluding the Petersen graph with one edge contracted'); v2 9 Aug 2026 (title 'Nowhere-zero 4-flows in graphs excluding a proper minor of the Petersen graph'; abstract adds the Thomas–Thomson combination). A Zenodo software deposit of verify_Q_minor.py dated 22 Jul 2026 (v1) predates the arXiv posting; the software is not a written argument, so the arXiv date is used. Whether v2's theorem text differs from v1 was not verified (the v2 PDF was unreadable here).
events.delivers: Nowhere-zero 4-flows for bridgeless multigraphs excluding P/e (a proper minor of P). Because P/e is a minor of P, every P/e-minor-free graph is P-minor-free, so this is a proper subclass of the bullet's class. Together with Thomas–Thomson (P−e), the author states it covers every class excluding a proper minor R of P. Carries the restriction to proper minors: the Petersen-minor-free class is not covered.
events.remains: Every bridgeless graph with no P minor that does contain a P/e minor (and so, equivalently, all graphs in the bullet's class not excluded by the P/e or P−e results). The Petersen graph itself is not excluded, so the bullet's class is not covered.
events.time_since_posted: 11 weeks (as of 11 Oct 2026); no public engagement found in searches

machine_checked.system: Author-written Python 3 verifier verify_Q_minor.py (standard library only), not a proof assistant; a successful run is said to end with ALL_CERTIFICATES_VALID

events.directly_checkable: The finite part: the Q = P/e minor models in the Petersen, Triplex and Basket graphs and the Dodecahedron extensions, checked by the deposited script (Zenodo, MIT licence). I did not run the script; it was not inspected beyond the Zenodo metadata and its filename.
events.doubts: Single author; one arXiv preprint; not peer reviewed or journal-published as far as found. The finite part depends on an author-written script, and no independent run or review was found. The AI disclosure names ChatGPT and Claude for code help (see ai). One search snippet described the result as reaching an intermediate 'P^(2)' class; the fetched v1 and v2 abstracts say P/e, so the snippet was not relied on.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive) for the proper-minor classes; it does not settle the Petersen-minor-free class, and it contains no counterexample.

The verifier verify_Q_minor.py is the likely referent, and the abstract makes the finite computer-assisted part part of the result, so this is a close call. The literature and editorial uses are not in the result.

events.what_happened: Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe, 'Three-edge-coloring apex cubic graphs', arXiv 2608.22870 (v1 submitted 24 Aug 2026; the only version listed). Theorem 1.4 (per the arXiv HTML): every 2-connected apex cubic graph (a vertex whose deletion leaves a planar graph) is 3-edge-colourable. The abstract says this 'gives the final piece of the proof for the well-known Tutte's three-edge-coloring conjecture from 1966', and the body says 'Together with Theorem 1.3 and [4], our result finally proves Tutte's three-edge-coloring conjecture'. Theorem 1.3 is the Robertson–Seymour–Thomas reduction (apex and doublecross suffice) and [4] is the 2016 doublecross result. The proof is constructive (O(n²) time) and computer-assisted: a reducibility and discharging procedure with pseudocode in the appendix, and source code on GitHub. The authors say 'the proof is computer-assisted' for Lemma 6.5. No formal proof assistant is mentioned.
events.delivers: Every 2-connected apex cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable. Per the authors, together with the RSST reduction and the 2016 doublecross result this proves Tutte's three-edge-colouring conjecture, i.e. the cubic special case of the bullet: every 2-connected cubic graph with no P minor is 3-edge-colourable, equivalently (for cubic graphs) has a nowhere-zero 4-flow. Cubic-restricted; the authors state the general 'Petersen-minor' condition only in their conjecture statement.
events.remains: The non-cubic bridgeless graphs with no P minor, which the preprint does not address. It also depends on the RSST reduction (announced, not published as one piece according to the Snark article) and on the apex-case result of Sanders, Seymour and Thomas (listed as 'in preparation' on Thomas's page), which this preprint does not cite as the source of its own proof.
events.time_since_posted: 7 weeks (as of 11 Oct 2026); no critique, endorsement or journal acceptance found in searches
events.directly_checkable: The computer-assisted part is checkable in principle from the GitHub source code and the appendix pseudocode, which the authors link. I did not inspect the repository.
events.doubts: (1) The apex case was announced around 30 years ago and never published, per the preprint itself. (2) The reduction (Theorem 1.3) is attributed to RSST, whose full proof the Snark article says remains unpublished. (3) The proof is computer-assisted with precomputed lookup tables and a discharging procedure; the authors offer independent reconstructions as a reproducibility check, which they say is not part of the mathematical justification. (4) The MathWorld entry hedges with 'if valid'. (5) Preprint, single version, about seven weeks old, with no public engagement found. None of these is an error identified; they are the grounds on which the claim is unrefereed.
events.direction: Cuts toward the conjecture (positive) for the cubic special case, if valid. It exhibits no counterexample and affirms the cubic form of the bullet's claim.

systems.name: GitHub Copilot
systems.what_it_did: Per the authors: used to assist in implementing parts of the authors' verification software. The authors say they reviewed all generated code and take responsibility for its correctness and for its match with the appendix pseudocode. The verification software produces the computer-assisted lemmas, so this is a close call: it is coding assistance rather than mathematics, but it is in the computational part of the result.
systems.basis_quote: GitHub Copilot was used to assist in implementing parts of the authors' verification software.

disputes.summary: Apex case: the Sanders–Thomas announcement (around 1996, per the 2026 preprint) with the Sanders–Seymour–Thomas paper 'in preparation' (Thomas's homepage), versus a 2016 Princeton mailing-list post saying Sanders and Thomas 'recently solved' the apex case, versus the 2026 preprint's own claim of the apex proof. No written apex argument before 2026 was located.

Full RSST proof: announced (1999 per the Snark article; undated on Thomas's homepage); the Snark article says steps were published in 2016 and 2019 and 'the complete proof remains unpublished'; a Waterloo thesis abstract (not opened) and an Open Problem Garden entry dated 2007 with 2009 comments say RSST 'proved' the cubic version. These conflict on whether the cubic case is settled.

Pintér's main theorem: the fetched v1 and v2 abstracts state P/e (Petersen with an edge contracted). One search snippet described the result as reaching an intermediate 'P^(2)' class and a 'largest of three excluded-minor classes'. The fetched text does not support that snippet, and it was not relied on.

summary: Nothing since 26 Jan 2024 settles the bullet for all Petersen-minor-free graphs. The two relevant 2026 preprints are: (a) Pintér, arXiv 2607.22267 (24 Jul 2026; v2 9 Aug 2026), whose main theorem (per the v1 HTML and the v2 abstract) gives nowhere-zero 4-flows for bridgeless multigraphs with no P/e minor; because P/e is a minor of P, this is a proper subclass of the bullet's class, and with the Thomas–Thomson (P−e, 2000) result it covers every proper-minor-excluded class. The author does not claim the full conjecture, and his own abstract states it as the open problem. The finite part is an author-written Python verifier (Zenodo, MIT), not a proof assistant, and no independent check was found. (b) Inoue, Kawarabayashi, Matsuo, Miyashita, Mohar and Sonobe, arXiv 2608.22870 (24 Aug 2026), which proves that every 2-connected apex cubic graph is 3-edge-colourable and says that with the RSST reduction (Theorem 1.3) and the 2016 doublecross result it 'finally proves' Tutte's 1966 three-edge-colouring conjecture. For cubic graphs a nowhere-zero 4-flow is equivalent to 3-edge-colourability, so this is the cubic special case of the bullet, claimed rather than accepted. The proof is computer-assisted (GitHub source, appendix pseudocode, no proof assistant). Its apex half was announced by Sanders and Thomas around 1996 and never published; the RSST reduction is announced, with only the 1997 JCTB paper and the 2014–2019 steps published; Thomas's page lists the SST apex paper as 'in preparation'. Searches turned up no critique, endorsement, or journal acceptance of the Inoue preprint in seven weeks. Close calls for AI involvement: (i) Inoue et al. credit GitHub Copilot with helping implement parts of the verification software, which I have put in ai.systems because it concerns code that produces computer-assisted lemmas, though it is coding help rather than mathematics. The same paper credits ChatGPT Pro and Gemini Deep Think with exposition help, and ChatGPT Pro and Claude Code with independent reconstructions of the computations; the authors state the reconstructions are not part of the mathematical justification. These are recorded here, not in ai.systems. (ii) Pintér credits OpenAI's ChatGPT and Anthropic's Claude with literature research, editorial help and 'help writing the accompanying code', without saying which code; I have listed both on the same quote, as close calls. Neither AI disclosure names a model version, and the quotes come from fetched text, so the exact wording should be checked against the PDFs. For the older events, none names an AI system (I read them at abstract or secondary-source level). The 2024 (projective-planar) and 2025 (toroidal) Inoue papers are analogue classes, not subclasses of the bullet: P is projective-planar and toroidal, so their hypotheses do not give P-minor-freeness. Other pre-window events are recorded with their scope: Kilakos–Shepherd (1996, cubic, secondary only), Kochol (1999, cubic 5-flow), Cahit (2005, unrefereed draft claiming a non-computer route), Taoye Zhang's dissertation and Wang–Zhang–Zhang (2007/2009, P/3-minor-free, a proper subclass), and Mkrtchyan (2020, withdrawn, a nullity equivalence). The Mattiolo (Nov 2025) and OpenAI cycle double cover (Jul 2026) items are different problems and are listed under dead ends.
competing_reading: Read Inoue et al. as completing the cubic special case: the bullet then has a claimed-settled cubic subcase and remains open for general graphs, and Pintér's result is a substantial partial result. That reading leans on the authors' own 'finally proves' sentence and on the computer checks. The strongest case against counting Inoue is that the apex half has never been published, the reduction's full proof is described as unpublished, the computer-assisted lemmas are not formally verified, and the preprint has had no public engagement in seven weeks. Read Pintér's 'every proper minor' framing as close to the full conjecture: it is not, because excluding P (the bullet) is weaker than excluding P/e or P−e, so the bullet's class contains graphs with P/e minors. Read the Copilot and ChatGPT/Claude mentions as load-bearing AI involvement: the authors call the Copilot help implementation work and call the reconstructions non-essential, so the stronger reading is a reading of the authors' own words against them.
what_would_settle_it: For the cubic subcase: a referee report or journal acceptance of arXiv 2608.22870; a published (or at least complete) version of the RSST reduction (Theorem 1.3); confirmation of the Sanders–Seymour–Thomas apex paper's status; an independent run of the GitHub verifier and a check of the Copilot-written code against the appendix pseudocode. For Pintér: journal publication, an independent run of verify_Q_minor.py (checking that ALL_CERTIFICATES_VALID is printed), a referee check of the girth-five lemma, and a read of the v2 full text to confirm no theorem changed between versions. For the general class (the bullet): a result covering bridgeless graphs with no P minor that contain a P/e minor. For AI: the exact wording and version of each AI disclosure in the PDFs (the Pintér 'accompanying code' sentence, and the Inoue Copilot sentence and the surrounding paragraph).
